items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: So he had the choice of either sending me to Adolf Alexander or Begaard. So he said, well I think I'd rather send you to Begaard.

ctx.x: mouthpiece from the horn that I had used. And do you find any difference in the tone between the two mouthpieces? Well, yes, I did. That's why I began using it. It made it a little broader because it was more of an open layer. But about the same kind of reed you've always used? Just a little softer reed. That's a soft. Now than what I had been using before.

I was using a much harder reed because the mouthpiece was a little closer. But the mouthpiece that was given to me by Begaard, by the layer being a little open, it made I use a softer reed. You know Begaard, when my father and I had gone to New York, well he taught me also. Oh yeah? Yeah. Because after they had gone and Lorenzo said he didn't want me to just be idling around and taking things on myself. So he had the choice of either sending me to Adolf Alexander or Begaard. So he said, well I think I'd rather…
Was there any particular thing that Lorenzo would teach you? For instance, would he teach you anything about tapping your foot? Yes.
